findings.summary: The base annotation 'slowest read 14.82 s' is drawn in the population grey #929292 and measures 3.11:1 on white, below the 4.5:1 a reader needs for 14 pt text. It is the only text in the figure below that bar (the bound label is 5.33:1 and the head annotation 5.42:1) and it labels the 'before' number the figure exists to show, so the least legible text carries the most important value; the figure still reads, which is why this does not hold the node.

Both arms plot five reads but the jitter that separates near-equal x, 0.065 in data units (about 9.5 px), is smaller than the marker diameter (about 11 px), so coincident reads merge into one elongated mark: head's 0.587, 0.594 and 0.606 s render as a single 12x29 px streak and the figure therefore shows three head marks where the alt text and the prose both say five, and base's 7.726 and 7.754 s merge likewise, leaving four base marks for five. The spread and the side of the bound still read correctly and the merged values differ by less than 30 ms, so this does not hold the node, but a reader cannot recover the sample size from the figure alone.

rubric_items.contrast: fails on one label - the base annotation 'slowest read 14.82 s' is #929292 and measures 3.11:1 against white, under the 4.5:1 its 14 pt text needs; the bound label #6b6b6b measures 5.33:1 and the head annotation #2b6cb0 5.42:1, so this is the single text artist below threshold and it labels the figure's headline before number.
rubric_items.data_ink: passes - the ink is seven visible marks, one dotted threshold line and five short labels on an otherwise empty white field; the marks are the darkest thing in each row and nothing larger or brighter than the record requires is drawn.
rubric_items.decoration: passes - there is no gradient, no shaded region, no marker edge or drop shadow and no background fill; the one dotted vertical rule is a data-carrying threshold and is labelled 'five-second bound', so it is data rather than styling.
rubric_items.label_collision: passes - no text is clipped (the rightmost label ends near x=1245 px of a 1400 px canvas, the row labels start inside the left edge) and no two text artists overlap: 'five-second bound' sits above and clear of all data, 'slowest read 1.42 s' is placed 0.55 s right of its mark and 'slowest read 14.82 s' ends 0.30 s left of its mark, each in clear space.
rubric_items.legibility: passes - at 1400x450 the row labels 'base' and 'head' sit at the left of two bands of marks, the axis reads 'read wall time [s]' with ticks every 2 s, and the picture reads in one glance: every head mark lies left of the dotted bound and every base mark right of it, with the slowest read of each arm named beside it, so which revision is faster and by how much is immediate.
rubric_items.table_form: passes - five repeated reads per arm compared against one threshold is a distribution-vs-bound question, and the dot plot shows the spread and the side of the bound that matters; a table of ten timings would carry the bound relation less directly.
